passages.title: Why Did The British Shift India's Capital From Kolkata To Delhi On This Day 113 Years Ago?
passages.passage:
Why Did The British Shift India's Capital From Kolkata To Delhi On This Day 113 Years Ago?
On December 11, 1911, the British colonial rulers in India had organised a grand Delhi Durbar, an event that marked a pivotal moment in the nation’s history. It was on this day that King George V, during his address at the Durbar, proposed a significant political change: the capital of India would shift from Kolkata (then Calcutta) to Delhi. The proposal was received with enthusiasm by the British, and the decision quickly gained unanimous support within their ranks. The very next day, December 12, 1911, in front of a gathering of over 80,000 people, King George V formally announced the relocation of the Indian capital to Delhi.
However, the transition from Kolkata to Delhi was not immediate. Despite the announcement, the practicalities of moving the seat of power were complicated. It was not until March 1931 that the British authorities fully embraced Delhi as the capital, formally leaving Kolkata behind. The shift was accompanied by great pomp and ceremony, a message to the world that Delhi, not Kolkata, would then serve as the heart of British India.

passages.title: 'Isro’s role won’t diminish': Agency allays concerns over privatisation
passages.passage:
'Isro’s role won’t diminish': Agency allays concerns over privatisation
Two days after nine associations representing thousands of Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) employees sought clarity on the privatisation of the space sector, IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka and Isro on Sunday said the space agency’s role would not diminish.
Goenka said there had been “some misleading narrative” in the media about Isro’s future role. “Let me say it unequivocally: ISRO’s role is by no means diminishing. It will remain the bedrock of Indian space sector. The reforms since 2020 are about expanding India’s overall space ecosystem,” he said in a post on X.
The employees’ associations had written to the Department of Space secretary and Isro chairman V Narayanan seeking clarity after Goenka said that “eventually, ISRO will not make any launch vehicles and will not manufacture any launch vehicles. That will all be done by the private sector or PSU.”
The agency said private-sector participation would enable the agency to focus on the next generation of India’s space programme while industry scales mature technologies.

Abhishek Sharma overtakes Virat Kohli for most T20 centuries by an Indian cricketer
Wellington [New Zealand], October 4 (ANI): Abhishek Sharma overtook Virat Kohli to become the Indian batter with the most T20 centuries on Tuesday. The explosive left-hander achieved this milestone during the third T20I against New Zealand at Wellington, scoring a 38-ball 113, with nine fours and 11 sixes at a strike rate of 297.37.Now, Abhishek, with 11 T20 centuries, has overtaken Virat's tally of 10 T20 centuries, becoming the Indian with the most T20 tonnes. Only West Indies titan Chris Gayle (22) and Pakistan batter Babar Azam (13) are above him, making him the third-highest centurion of all time in T20s already. Abhishek now has four T20I centuries, the joint second-highest in T20I history, levelling with stars like Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav and England's Phil Salt. passages.passage:
Chandrayaan-3 May Have Landed On Moon's Oldest Craters, Says Researchers
India's lunar mission Chandrayaan-3 possibly landed in one of the oldest craters of the Moon, according to scientists who analysed images from the mission and satellites.
S Vijayan, an associate professor in the Planetary Sciences Division, Physical Research Laboratory, told PTI, "Chandrayaan-3 landing site is a unique geological setting where no other missions have gone. The images from the mission's Pragyan rover are the first on-site ones of the Moon at this latitude. They reveal how the Moon evolved over time".
In this case, Chandrayaan-3 was found to have landed within a crater -- about 160 km in diameter -- and detected in the images as a nearly semi-circular structure.
The Pragyan rover was deployed on the lunar surface by the Vikram lander, on board the Chandrayaan-3.
"Together, the images from the mission and satellites showed that the Chandrayaan-3 landing site consists of material deposited from different regions of the Moon," he said.

passages.title: Chandrayaan-3 rover lands in oldest crater where ‘no other missions have gone’; S.Vijayan says ‘shows how moon evolved'
passages.passage:
Chandrayaan-3 rover lands in oldest crater where ‘no other missions have gone’; S.Vijayan says ‘shows how moon evolved'
Chandrayaan 3: India's lunar mission has landed in one of the oldest craters on the Moon, scientists said on Saturday. The crater where ‘no other missions’ have gone, is 3.85 billion years old, said scientists.
“Chandrayaan-3 landing site is a unique geological setting where no other missions have gone. The images from the mission's Pragyan rover are the first on-site ones of the Moon at this latitude. They reveal how the Moon evolved,” said Vijayan, reported PTI.
An impact basin is defined as a large, complex crater with a diameter exceeding 300 km, whereas a regular crater is less than 300 km in diameter. In this instance, Chandrayaan-3 was found to have landed within a crater approximately 160 km wide, appearing in images as a nearly semi-circular structure.
On August 23, 2023, Chandrayaan-3 made a soft landing on the Moon's south pole. The GOI named the landing site as ‘Shiv Shakti Point’.

Diljit has now landed in the French capital and given fans a glimpse of his time in the city. Taking to social media, the Punjabi superstar shared a video featuring one of Paris' most recognisable landmarks – the Eiffel Tower.
The Eiffel Tower is among the most famous landmarks in the world and has become synonymous with Paris. Standing at 330 metres (1,083 feet), the tower was originally planned as a 300-metre structure for the 1889 Exposition Universelle, a world fair organised to mark the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution.
All the elements were prepared in Eiffel's factory located at Levallois-Perret on the outskirts of Paris. The structure was assembled using prefabricated metal components. According to the official Eiffel Tower website, around 18,000 individual metal parts were specifically designed and calculated, traced out to an accuracy of a tenth of a millimetre and then put together, forming new pieces around five metres each.

Bitcoin's rebound was short-lived after the midterm results in early November. Bitcoin was trading near $77,500 before voters went to the polls on November 3. Immediately following the November 3, 2026, US midterm elections, Bitcoin briefly rallied to a peak near $81,196. It fell to an intraday low of about $75,630 on November 4, after Democrats won control of Congress, amid concern that the result could slow new crypto legislation. It quickly recovered, climbing above $80,000 and briefly topping $81,000. The gains did not last. A hotter-than-expected October inflation and looming interest rate hike reading pushed Bitcoin below $74,000, and it had slipped under $73,000 by November 11,The pullback arrives as analysts debate whether the post-election period will follow history. Bitcoin rose 24.5% in the 12 months after the 2014 midterms, 44.9% after 2018 and 92.3% after 2022. Past bottoms came 13 to 71 days after those elections. ISRO further provided the launch pad at Sriharikota and hand held the company during vehicle assembly and launch operations.
This was not the first time ISRO opened its doors to a private launch company.

passages.title: Is Indian space agency being privatised? ISRO chief V Narayanan clarifies role of private sector in space missions
passages.passage:
Is Indian space agency being privatised? ISRO chief V Narayanan clarifies role of private sector in space missions
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has rejected speculation about privatising the space agency. Chairman V Narayanan reiterated that “people must not misinterpret that ISRO will be privatised”. He stated that a large chunk of the space agency’s budget goes to the private sector to meet surging global and domestic demand for thousands of satellites.
“The space ecosystem in the country and the country’s economy will grow, resulting in job opportunities. When a Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) or Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) rocket takes off, 75% of our budget is pumped into the private industries. The private companies are also contributing. People must not misinterpret that as ISRO will be privatised,” Narayanan was quoted as saying by The Hindu.
"To handle this expanding ecosystem, ISRO will handhold startups and private enterprises, transferring technological expertise to foster economic growth and generate thousands of high-tech jobs," he said at the graduation ceremony at a private university in the city on Saturday.

passages.title: India’s top-funded space startup tees up for country’s 1st private rocket launch
passages.passage:
India’s top-funded space startup tees up for country’s 1st private rocket launch
Now, three years after India opened up its space sector to private companies, Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace is targetting its first full-scale commercial satellite launch mission by January.
Skyroot, co-founded by two former Isro scientists, is targetting one launch every three months next year, and one every month from 2027. Each satellite launch mission is expected to generate the company nearly $5 million, according to Skyroot chief executive Pawan Chandana.
While SpaceX, the Elon Musk-owned private space company, has been able to drastically lower the cost of rocket launches, it has a long wait list of almost two years—making it difficult for companies to use its services.

passages.title: Inside Skyroot India’s first private rocket factory
passages.passage:
The blast of air conditioning hit me instantly as I stepped in. The floors were squeaky clean. The space was decked in off-white, with elaborately designed seating areas that looked like a spaceship module, straight from the sets of some sci-fi film. Glass cabins were labelled Mars, Venus, Orion. The quiet mood reflected seriousness and precision.
“It was a huge learning experience and gave us instant exposure to the rigours of building and developing a rocket,” Bharath recalls. “We were also closely tracking developments in the private space ecosystem. Rocket Lab in New Zealand, which carried out its maiden launch in 2017, was a major inspiration. India already rubs shoulders with the world in space technology. We have a strong ecosystem and manufacturing base, and we believe we could do it too. That’s when we took the leap, leaving Isro and starting Skyroot in 2018.”
In 2022, Skyroot made its mark as the first private company in India to launch a suborbital rocket, Vikram-S. As it soared from a mobile launchpad in Sriharikota, the startup realised it was on the right track. With every milestone Vikram-S rocket crossed, the data showed they had nailed the science.

passages.passage:
Chandrayaan-3 May Have Landed On Moon's Oldest Craters, Says Researchers
India's lunar mission Chandrayaan-3 possibly landed in one of the oldest craters of the Moon, according to scientists who analysed images from the mission and satellites.
S Vijayan, an associate professor in the Planetary Sciences Division, Physical Research Laboratory, told PTI, "Chandrayaan-3 landing site is a unique geological setting where no other missions have gone. The images from the mission's Pragyan rover are the first on-site ones of the Moon at this latitude. They reveal how the Moon evolved over time".
In this case, Chandrayaan-3 was found to have landed within a crater -- about 160 km in diameter -- and detected in the images as a nearly semi-circular structure.
The Pragyan rover was deployed on the lunar surface by the Vikram lander, on board the Chandrayaan-3.
"Together, the images from the mission and satellites showed that the Chandrayaan-3 landing site consists of material deposited from different regions of the Moon," he said.

Chandrayaan-3, India's lunar mission, has landed in a 3.85-billion-year-old crater on the Moon, scientists said on Saturday. The crater is one of the oldest on the Moon's surface.
The scientists, including those from the Physical Research Laboratory and Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Ahmedabad, said that the crater where Chandrayaan-3 landed was formed during the Nectarian period, about 3.85 billion years ago.
"Chandrayaan-3 landing site is a unique geological setting where no other missions have gone. The images from the mission's Pragyan rover are the first on-site ones of the Moon at this latitude. They reveal how the Moon evolved," he told PTI.
In this case, Chandrayaan-3 was found to have landed within a crater -- about 160 km in diameter -- and detected in the images as a nearly semi-circular structure.
The Chandrayaan-3 made a soft landing on the Moon's south pole on August 23, 2023. It is the only mission to have landed on the south side of the Moon. The government calls the landing site Shiv Shakti Point., three days later.

While addressing the NAACP’s annual convention, Joe Biden teased that vice president Kamala Harris “could be president of the United States.” This comes as Biden faces growing calls to drop out of the race.
“She’s not only a great vice president, she could be president of the United States,” Biden, 81, said.
Were Biden to step aside, Harris would be the most obvious presidential pick. However, she has often been criticised for not being unable to form her own role in the Biden administration, and also has poor approval ratings. But should Biden choose to resign, it is Harris who would be best-positioned to replace him.
However, Biden gave no indication that he plans to drop out. In fact, the president told the crowd that he has already made plans for the first 100 days of a second term, and one of them would be to sign voting-rights legislation “come hell or high water.”

passages.title: Joe Biden Joins Protesting Auto Workers, First For Sitting US President

Joe Biden Joins Protesting Auto Workers, First For Sitting US President
US President Joe Biden joined striking auto workers on the picket line in Michigan Tuesday in a historic first for a sitting US president, a day before rival Donald Trump makes his own bid for the blue-collar vote in the battleground electoral state.
The current and former presidents are both targeting the blue-collar vote in Michigan, a key swing state that Trump won in 2016 and then Biden flipped back in 2020.
Biden has consistently talked up his pro-union credentials, and an endorsement from the United Auto Workers (UAW) union helped him secure the presidency three years ago.
However, Biden says his push for electric vehicles is part of a plan to bring manufacturing jobs back to the United States and put the country in the lead of a global race to develop green technology.
The White House deflected a barrage of questions about whether Biden was taking sides in the dispute, saying the president wanted a "win-win" agreement and would not get involved in negotiations.

New Delhi, Nov 19 (PTI) In a “major milestone” in the fight against terrorism, Kashmir is free from India-born terrorists after 35 years, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday and stressed the need to strengthen “proactive action” in the country’s counter-terrorism policy.
Shah credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ‘zero-tolerance’ policy towards terrorism for yielding decisive results on the ground.
To eliminate the three menaces of terrorism, organised crime, and drugs, it is essential to bring the culprits and masterminds who have taken shelter abroad before Indian courts, Shah said.

"Winning or losing elections depends on the performance of political parties and their leaders. The Congress got an opportunity to govern the country for 10 years (2004-14), but during its tenure, corruption of Rs 12 lakh crore took place. People eventually voted the party out of power and brought Narendra Modi to the Prime Minister's Office," Shah said.

"If he aspires to return to power, he should stop travelling abroad and start visiting villages across India. Then, perhaps, he may have a chance," Shah said.

The summit was named Bharat, but its platform was used to criticise the Prime Minister and the country. We strongly condemn this,” Shah said.

As millions stayed awake through the night in early July to watch Cabo Verde’s spirited performance against defending champions Argentina at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, football fans in India wondered how a tiny archipelago off the coast of Africa, only slightly bigger than Goa, is squaring up against footballing giants, while even qualifying for the tournament remains a distant dream for India. The sorry state of Indian football showed when India was forced to withdraw from the 2026 Asian Games because the men’s team failed to satisfy the Union sports ministry’s criterion of being among Asia’s top eight. India ranks 24 among the 46 members of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and the team failed to qualify yet again for the AFC Asian Cup 2027, the foremost competition in the continent. India’s quest to make history collapsed in 2024 itself in the second round of the AFC qualifiers. Competing in Group A alongside Qatar, Kuwait and Afghanistan, it failed to secure a top two finish needed to progress in the World Cup qualifiers. The Blue Tigers managed just one win—against Kuwait—their first away win in 22 years.

Dhaka: A mob damaged 66 houses and set on fire at least 20 homes of Hindus in Bangladesh over an alleged blasphemous social media post amidst protests by the minority community against temple vandalism incidents during the Durga Puja celebrations, authorities said on Monday. The police rushed to a fishermen neighbourhood as tension mounted over a rumour that a young Hindu man of the village had ‘dishonoured religion’ in a Facebook post, Assistant Police Superintendent Mohammad Kamruzzaman said. “The incident took place after 10 pm on Sunday but firefighters doused the blaze within a short period. passages.passage:
Military bases capable of operating for three months without external resupply, independent power sources, nuclear microreactors, and huge stockpiles of critical materials. These are among the measures included in the US Pentagon’s plans to strengthen the resilience of American military facilities against cyberattacks, sabotage, and the possible collapse of vital infrastructure.
The program was officially announced on September 30 by US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, during a speech at the Marine Corps base in Quantico, Virginia. The name FORTRESS comes from the initials of the words Federal Operations for Resilience, Troop Resources, Energy, Supply and Survivability, describing a network of federal operations covering resilience, military resources, energy, supply, and survivability.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell explained that electricity has now become a critical factor in military power. Is the US preparing for a 90-day blackout? What the Pentagon's FORTRESS America plan actually means
The doomsday and nationwide blackout rumors started circulating after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth revealed the Pentagon's long-term readiness initiative on September 30, per Fox News. The preparation that would allow US military bases to keep operating for at least 90 days without any outside support is a requirement that's part of the FORTRESS America plan.
Under FORTRESS, every major military installation across the US would be expected to be able to sustain its essential operations for 90 days. That includes having access to water, electricity, fuel, and communications. According to the memorandum that the Secretary of War released on September 30:
The FORTRESS America plan is not an announcement of an active nationwide blackout in the US or a power cut that could last for up to 90 days and affect American citizens. Rather, it's the country's prepared plan to ensure that the US's military power "cannot be starved out, shut down, or cut off."

passages.title: Future astronauts wanted: NASA opens recruitment for moon missions
passages.passage:
Artist’s concept of living and working at Moon Base. Credit: NASA
NASA wants to find the men and women who will help forge the next chapter in the history of space exploration. On Saturday, the space agency put out the call for a new astronaut class, one that will build humanity’s first permanent lunar base.
"The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said. "Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage."
Anyone looking to become an astronaut has until Dec. 3 to apply. NASA intends to have its recruits picked by late next year, with the goal of beginning training in early 2028, the same year it hopes to return people to the moon for the first time since the days of the Apollo program.
NASA only has 32 active astronauts and needs more for the coming missions. The last time NASA opened its doors to new astronauts was two years ago, and the agency was flooded with 8,000 applications. Ten of those applicants made the final cut, which was decided in Sept. 2025.

NASA has begun selecting new astronaut candidates to participate in flights to the Moon, work on its surface, and prepare for future Mars missions. Selected candidates may participate in upcoming missions under the Artemis program, as well as contribute to establishing long-term human presence on the Moon.
According to NASA, applicants to become astronauts must be U.S. citizens and hold a master's degree in a STEM field from an accredited higher education institution. This includes fields such as engineering, biology, physics, and computer science.
In addition, candidates must successfully pass NASA's long-duration spaceflight physical examination and possess leadership, teamwork, and communication skills.
Applications will be accepted until 11:59 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on December 3, 2026. NASA plans to select the new astronaut candidates by the end of 2027.
The agency notes that the new generation of astronauts may participate in working on the lunar surface, ensuring a permanent human presence there in the future, and developing the experience and technologies necessary for crewed flights to Mars.

Premium headphones are cool, but for some people, a solid pair of midrange headphones can be a better fit. Bose gifted its midrange headphones with several key upgrades previously exclusive to its premium headphones, including USB-C audio, adaptive noise-canceling technology, and spatial audio. The second-gen QuietComfort Headphones retain their $359 price tag — for now.
Bose upgraded several audio features of the QuietComfort Headphones, including USB-C audio. Users can listen in 24-bit/48kHz lossless resolution via USB-C and charge the headphones while they’re in use. passages.passage:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.
Bose is adding a new pair of headphones to its lineup. The new QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) are the successor to the 2023 model, and the more affordable alternative to the flagship QuietComfort Ultra headphones. Announced today, the headphones cost $359 at launch. They’ll be available to buy on Aug. 8 and ship on Aug. 13, and they come in black, white smoke, eucalyptus green, dewdrop mint, and rosewood mauve.
Some of the bigger changes are under the hood, with Bose adding features from its flagship model to this more budget-friendly pair. You now get new “Immersion” and “Cinema” modes, which were previously only available on the Ultra model. The QuietComfort Headphones also now have ActiveSense, which turns up noise-canceling when there are sudden loud noises.
You’ll be able to preorder the new headphones on Aug. 8. Meanwhile, the second-gen QuietComfort Ultra headphones are currently discounted to $399. And it’s likely that the first-gen QuietComfort headphones will also get a discount once the latest iteration hits the market.

passages.title: I tested Bose’s new QuietComfort headphones, and one upgrade stole the show
passages.passage:
I’ve long been a fan of Bose headphones and earbuds, even giving the brand’s open-ear design a chance.
Bose launched the previous generation of its standard QuietComfort Headphones in 2023. The brand followed those with the Ultra, a more luxe upgrade to the originals, but at the time, the Ultra was the only Bose headphone pair with spatial audio for a more immersive listening experience.
Starting with the basics, I love the case and foldable design. The Bose QuietComfort 2nd Gen headphones are also extremely lightweight, weighing just over half a pound, so they feel like nothing when they’re on your head. That said, the earcups are a little smaller, which I was initially worried about, but surprisingly, I haven’t experienced any sound leakage.
I love my new Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), but probably for an entirely different reason than they’re intended for. While I use them on my commute because the noise cancellation is brilliant, they act as a lifestyle accessory for me almost as much as a traditional pair of headphones.

passages.passage:
Balochistan declares August 11 as Independence Day, renews call for global recognition after breaking away from Pakistan
Weeks after declaring independence from Pakistan, the self-proclaimed Republic of Balochistan on Monday announced that August 11 would be observed as the Independence Day of Balochistan and appealed to Baloch communities across the world to mark the occasion with nationwide celebrations, reported CNN-News18.
In a statement, the Republic of Balochistan called on the international community to recognise what it described as an independent and sovereign Balochistan, while urging people across the Baloch nation to commemorate the day with unity.
According to the statement, the Republic of Balochistan regards August 11 as its Independence Day and said the occasion would be observed every year.
The Republic of Balochistan announces worldwide celebrations of August 11 as the Independence Day of Balochistan with national unity 3 August, 2026 On this occasion, the residents of the Baloch nation will hoist the national flag of independent Balochistan in their homes,… pic.twitter.com/CsDZqWAC8x

passages.title: Republic Day vs Independence Day: Why Jan 26 gets the grander celebration than Aug 15
passages.passage:
Republic Day vs Independence Day: Why Jan 26 gets the grander celebration than Aug 15
While Independence Day is dominated by the Prime Minister’s address from the Red Fort, Republic Day is associated with a massive parade featuring the armed forces, military hardware, cultural tableaux and an elaborate ceremonial programme. So, why does Republic Day appear to be celebrated with greater pomp and pageantry?
India became independent from British rule on August 15, 1947. The day marks the culmination of a long freedom struggle and the transfer of power from the British to an independent Indian government.
Independence Day is therefore primarily a celebration of freedom from colonial rule.
That makes Republic Day a celebration not just of independence, but of the constitutional framework through which independent India governs itself.
The celebrations also traditionally include a foreign dignitary as the chief guest, giving Republic Day an important diplomatic dimension.

passages.title: Why Is August 11 Chosen As Baloch Independence Day?
passages.passage:
Why Is August 11 Chosen As Baloch Independence Day?
The history of Baloch independence dates back even before 1947, when it was under the rule of the Khanate of Kalat. In 1876, Kalat concluded a unique treaty with the British Crown.
Whereas Pakistan celebrates its liberation on August 14, Baloch nationalists prefer August 11 in order to commemorate their brief independent state.
The nationalist groups in Balochistan celebrated their Independence Day on August 11, 2026, by asking the United Nations and the international community for diplomatic recognition of their sovereignty. People such as Mir Yar Baloch asked for help in supporting the sovereignty of their people. At the same time, the Pakistani government was using tough methods by digging defence trenches around military bases.

A strong earthquake of magnitude 6.4 jolted Japan’s Ishikawa and other central Japan prefectures on Tuesday, the country’s weather agency said.
According to the preliminary information, the earthquake occurred at a depth of around 10 km off the western coast of the prefecture measuring a lower 5 on the Japanese seismic scale of 7 in Ishkiwara’s Noto, a region which is still recovering from the deadly January 1 earthquakes.
The Japanese Meteorological Agency (JMA) had said that at least 155 earthquakes along with the aforementioned 7.5-magnitude earthquake (and the 6-magnitude aftershock that followed closely after) struck Japan on January 1.
The massive earthquake had toppled buildings, triggered landslides and sparked a massive fire. Video footage shared on social media and also shared by Japanese local news outlets showed restaurant doors and street signs shaking due to the intensity of the earthquake. At a karaoke bar in Ishikawa, people were heard crying for help as tables were recorded shaking intensely following the earthquake, spilling drinks from glasses.

passages.passage:
At least 20 people were injured after a 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Japan early on Sunday, local media reported.
Kyodo News reported injuries in Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures, citing local authorities.
The earthquake originated in the western part of Shizuoka prefecture at a depth of about 40 kilometres (25 miles), according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
The quake was the strongest to hit Aichi in about three decades.
A 4.3 magnitude earthquake hit the Kumamoto prefecture in southwestern Japan on Sunday morning.
Japan, which sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and directly atop four major tectonic plates, is one of the most seismically active countries in the world.

Magnitude 5.7 Earthquake Hits Central Japan, Injuring Over 20 and Delaying High-Speed Rail
A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck central Japan early Sunday, injuring dozens of residents and causing widespread transit delays across key transportation corridors. The tremor occurred at 1:04 a.m.
local time on Sunday, November 8, 2026 (16:04 GMT on Saturday, November 7), according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
Local authorities across Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures reported that at least 20 to 24 people sustained injuries during the shaking. Officials noted that the injuries primarily resulted from falls, accidents on stairs, and individuals tumbling from their beds as the ground shook in the middle of the night.
The earthquake temporarily disrupted high-speed rail operations in Japan's central economic corridor. The Tokaido Shinkansen bullet train operated at reduced speeds between Shizuoka and Gifu-Hashima while personnel conducted track and safety inspections, before returning to normal-speed service before noon on Sunday.

More than 20 people were injured after a 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Japan early on Sunday, shaking buildings, shattering shop windows and sending residents rushing out of their homes. No tsunami warning was issued following the tremor.
The earthquake struck at around 1.04 am local time, with its epicentre in western Shizuoka Prefecture at a depth of approximately 40 km, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA).
According to a report by Japan Today, the strongest shaking was recorded in Aichi Prefecture. The city of Chita experienced an upper 5 on Japan's seven-level seismic intensity scale. Tremors were also felt in neighbouring Nagano and Gifu prefectures.
At least 22 people were injured, according to the latest updates. Some sustained injuries while attempting to evacuate buildings during the earthquake.
The earthquake caused damage in several affected areas, with shop windows shattered and broken glass scattered across streets.

Neil Bush noted Paxton's impeachment by the Republican-controlled Texas House and later acquittal by the Texas Senate, but said his vote for Talarico, a former teacher and state lawmaker, was "about much more" than his opposition to Paxton.
Former president George W. Bush's daughter, Barbara Bush, reportedly donated to a super PAC supporting Talarico's Senate bid.

As we have noted on multiple occasions, including during the Sixth Committee’s consideration of a new request for observer status several weeks ago, the United States believes it is time for the United Nations to get back to basics, to renew its founding mission to maintain international peace and security, and to rebuild trust across the world that the UN can be a responsible steward of the precious resources that Member States entrust to it. In that context, we believe that “getting back to basics” includes taking a more disciplined approach to considering organizations’ requests for observer status in the General Assembly.
Turning to the specific request[s] up for consideration today, we note that General Assembly Decision 49/426 limits the types of organizations that can be granted observer status in the General Assembly to “intergovernmental organizations whose activities cover matters of interest to the Assembly.”

passages.passage:
An official website of the United States government
Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States.
As previously noted, General Assembly Decision 49/426 limits the types of organizations that can be granted observer status in the General Assembly to “intergovernmental organizations whose activities cover matters of interest to the Assembly.” Unfortunately, the United States is unable at this time to support the request to grant observer status to the Climate Vulnerable Forum, or CVF. We have outstanding questions regarding whether the CVF is an intergovernmental organization under international law as required by Decision 49/426. We note that the sponsorship letter submitted in support of the CVF states that the Forum has “juridical personality” in light of a headquarters agreement between the Forum itself and the Government of the Republic of Ghana. Chetwode, Dinkar to a Field Marshal’s baton: How the Army chief’s office has changed
The longest-standing fixture in the Army chief’s office was Field Marshal Philip W Chetwode’s motto, delivered by him at the inauguration of the Indian Military Academy in Dehradun in 1932.
Chetwode’s words remained on the wall for decades, including during General VP Malik’s tenure as Army chief from 1997 to 2000, Malik confirmed to HT.
Dinkar’s verses made way for the Field Marshal’s baton under the current Army chief, General Dhiraj Seth. Portraits of the two military legends have also been replaced with newer versions, recasting the corner as a tribute to India’s Field Marshals.
Seth has made another change. In the adjacent Army chief’s lounge, the painting titled Karam Kshetra—Field of Deeds has been replaced by the Indian Army emblem. The Karam Kshetra artwork had replaced an iconic painting depicting the signing of the Instrument of Surrender at the end of the 1971 war with Pakistan, which led to the liberation of Bangladesh.

The user likely wanted to invite a discussion on the merits and demerits of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR), which India is building in collaboration with Japan, but, perhaps, did not anticipate that one of the responses would be from Railway Minister Piyush Goyal himself. These trains are expected to be comparable to Japan’s next-generation E10 series, with production of the Japanese trains also scheduled to begin in the same year. It is important to note that the proposal was part of the approval process for the revised cost of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project.
Excluding the Japanese trains that are expected to arrive in the future, the current project cost works out to around Rs 399 crore per kilometre. Initially, B28 trains will operate on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor. These trains will have a design speed of 280 kmph, while their maximum operating speed will be 249 kmph.
BEML has been awarded a contract to manufacture 32 B28 trains. Two prototype trains are expected to be ready for trial runs by the first quarter of 2027. On Friday, BEML informed the BSE that it had received a separate Rs 5,400 crore contract to manufacture 15 additional B28 trains.

Tesla Working On New Smaller, Cheaper Electric Vehicle: Report
Electric vehicle major Tesla is reportedly developing an all-new, compact electric SUV that would be smaller and significantly cheaper than its current entry-level models, according to a Reuters report. The project is said to mark a renewed push into the affordable EV segment, coming two years after CEO Elon Musk had shelved an earlier low-cost EV programme widely associated with the so called "Model 2" concept.
To achieve a lower price tag, the vehicle is expected to feature a smaller battery pack, which would translate into a shorter driving range compared with the Model Y's roughly 526 km. It is also likely to be offered with a single electric motor, instead of the dual-motor configuration found on many current Tesla models, further helping to reduce complexity and cost. The car is projected to be priced substantially below the Model 3 positioning it more clearly in the mass-market segment.

Tesla is scheduled to report its third-quarter financial results on Oct. 21.

Argentina's poverty rate increased to 32.3 percent in the first half of 2026, partly erasing gains made under President Javier Milei as incomes fail to keep step with rising prices, official statistics showed Thursday.
The rate grew 4.1 points compared to the last half of 2025, the national statistics agency Indec said.
The rate of extreme poverty also shot up from 6.3 percent to 7.5 percent.

The median U.S. household income went up 2.6% in 2025 from the previous year, after adjusting for inflation, to $87,460, according to the Census Bureau. That’s a record high, topping the 2019 household income of $85,320. Even though there are more people living below the poverty line than there have been in past years, the official poverty rate is lower because of population growth. There were 34.51 million people living below the poverty line in 2025, compared with an all-time low of 22.97 million in 1973. But while the 2025 number is larger, the U.S. population was 11.54 million higher, which drove down the rate.

passages.title: Trump Touts Record - Low U . S . Poverty Rate | Power 620 | Steve Harvey Morning Show
passages.passage:
Want to know more about Steve Harvey Morning Show? Get their official bio, social pages & articles on The Steve Harvey Morning Show!Full Bio
President Donald Trump is highlighting newly released economic data showing that the official U.S. poverty rate has fallen to its lowest level on record.
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the official poverty rate fell to 10.2% in 2025, the lowest level since the government began tracking the measure in 1959.
The decline marked the second consecutive year that the official poverty rate decreased.
However, a record-low poverty rate does not mean poverty has disappeared. Approximately 34.5 million Americans were still living below the official poverty line in 2025.
The official poverty rate is also only one measure of Americans’ economic circumstances. Families can still experience financial pressure from housing, food, health care, transportation and other expenses even when their income places them above the federal poverty threshold.

passages.title: Argentine poverty rate climbs , in setback for Milei
passages.passage:
Argentine poverty rate climbs, in setback for Milei
Argentina's poverty rate increased to 32.3 percent in the first half of 2026, partly erasing gains made under President Javier Milei as incomes fail to keep step with rising prices, official statistics showed.
The rate grew 4.1 points compared to the last half of 2025, the national statistics agency Indec said on Sept. 24.
The rate of extreme poverty also shot up from 6.3 percent to 7.5 percent.
The figures deal a setback to Milei, a free-market radical, who nearly halved the poverty rate during the first two years of his mandate, mainly by shrinking perennially high inflation.
From a high of 52.9 percent in the first half of 2024, following his more-than-50-percent devaluation of the peso, the rate fell to 28.2 percent in the second half of 2025.

Who is Erika Kirk, Charlie Kirk’s widow and new CEO of Turning Point USA?
Turning Point USA announced on September 18 that Erika Kirk, the widow of its co-founder Charlie Kirk, has been unanimously elected as the organisation’s new Chief Executive Officer and chair of the board. The board noted that Charlie Kirk had privately expressed the wish that his wife succeed him if he were unable to continue, saying he had “prepared all of us for a moment like this.”
Turning Point USA is a U.S. conservative youth organisation co-founded by Charlie Kirk in 2012. It grew into one of America’s most influential right-wing campus groups, with chapters on hundreds of college and high school campuses nationwide. The group describes its mission as promoting conservative ideas among students; it has attracted millions of followers through campus events, social media, and summer training programmes.
On September 10, 2025, Charlie Kirk died after being shot while speaking at a Turning Point USA event at Utah Valley University.

Founded when Charlie was just 18, Turning Point USA has since grown into a prominent political force with a presence on hundreds of college and high school campuses. Chev Clarke Stops Chris Billam-Smith In Round 7 At Zuffa Boxing 12 (Highlights)
Clarke broke through in the seventh after six rounds left two judges level, earning Performance of the Night recognition in London.
Chev Clarke defeated Chris Billam-Smith by TKO at 1:24 of Round 7 in the Zuffa Boxing 12 main event on November 7. The cruiserweight contest at London’s Copper Box Arena ended with the former world champion unable to escape Clarke’s finishing attack.
Both arrived with momentum from Zuffa Boxing 7 in Bournemouth. Billam-Smith had beaten Ryan Rozicki when the corner stopped their fight in the seventh. Clarke’s route was more precarious: he recovered from two knockdowns against Jack Massey before securing his own seventh-round stoppage.
The promotion’s preview traced their rivalry back to the amateur ranks, including Clarke’s decision victory in a National Championships final a decade earlier. The professional meeting offered Billam-Smith a different opportunity to reverse that history. For Clarke, defeating someone who had already held a world championship offered a more substantial test than simply renewing an old acquaintance.

CHEV CLARKE blew Chris Billam-Smith off the air with an explosive seventh-round stoppage to complete a hat-trick of wins over his old amateur rival.
The man nicknamed C4 detonated a devastating overhand right that sent the former WBO cruiserweight world champion crashing to the canvas at London’s Copper Box Arena.

The Indian and Chinese armies on Sunday held corps commander-level talks at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh’s Kibithoo sector, days after the two countries held the 25th round of talks between their special representatives on the boundary issue in Beijing.
Lieutenant General Girish Kalia, who heads the Dimapur-based 3 Corps, led the Indian side. The Army did not comment on the development.
Sunday’s meeting was also the first since tensions reportedly erupted between the Indian Army and the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) in Taksin, a remote area of Arunachal Pradesh’s Upper Subansiri district.
The status of the standoff reported in the Arunachal Pradesh sector is unclear. However, people familiar with the situation had earlier said there were a few face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in the Taksin area and that matters became more serious towards the end of July.

Did China capture 50 km of Arunachal? Army debunks claims, flags Pak-run campaign
The Indian Army has debunked social media claims that Chinese forces defeated Indian troops, advanced nearly 50 km into Arunachal Pradesh and brought parts of Indian territory under the control of the People's Liberation Army (PLA).
Under the heading "Coordinated Inauthentic Behaviour Exposed", the Army said the posts falsely alleged a major Chinese incursion into Arunachal Pradesh.
The posts repeat claims about Chinese troops advancing 50 km into Arunachal Pradesh and taking control of the area, alongside videos showing soldiers in a wooded, rocky landscape.

passages.passage: Chronic pain is a complex health condition wherein persistent pain is experienced for months, even years, without a definite cause. According to the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and affiliated bodies like the National Centre for Disease Informatics and Research (NCDIR), chronic pain is emerging as a major public health issue in India due to the startling figures. The figures indicate a steep rise, as about 19 to 25% of Indian adults report chronic pain lasting more than 3 months. Out of this figure, women are disproportionately affected, with the recorded rates nearly 1.5 times higher than men, especially pain in the bones, muscles, joints, tendons, and ligaments, and due to nervous system dysfunction.

passages.title: Covid-19 lockdowns caused more chronic pain in women than men. Here's why
passages.passage:
Covid-19 lockdowns caused more chronic pain in women than men. Here's why
A new study has found that the pandemic lockdown caused an increase in chronic pain, especially in women.
"With chronic pain affecting around 20 per cent of the EU adult population, it is vital to understand how people living with chronic pain are being affected by the pandemic and to develop pain management interventions that clearly target women," Lang-Illievich added.
Responses indicated that women with chronic pain perceived increased pain severity during the first lockdown, compared to their typical pain levels prior to lockdown. While average pain intensity scored (VAS 0-100) before the first COVID-19 lockdown was similar in men (46.5) and women (45), the average change in pain intensity was much lower in men (0.8) than women (3.9).
"Although reported pain intensity between men and women was similar before COVID-19, our data clearly show that women experienced a higher aggravation of chronic pain during the first lockdown," said Lang-Illievich.

passages.title: 5 ways Europe could revamp its security architecture to please Putin and Trump
passages.passage:
BRUSSELS — The U.S. and Russia are pressing Europe to overhaul the continent’s security architecture in a bid to end the war in Ukraine — and that could mean anything from giving Moscow a bigger say to no change at all.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has long insisted on a rethink of European defense, demanding that NATO pull back its forces and that Russia be given a key voice in the continent's security — calls that predate the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
“Security guarantees for Ukraine cannot be finalized in isolation from post-war European security architecture. The two must be considered together,” Trump's peace envoy Jared Kushner wrote Sunday.
The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, headquartered in Vienna, is one of the few European security bodies Russia still belongs to.
“We need to make full use of this unique platform to preserve dialogue, rebuild transparency, reduce risks and manage tensions,” OSCE Secretary-General Feridun Sinirlioğlu told POLITICO. “The OSCE remains a key forum for rebuilding a more stable and predictable security architecture in Europe.”

passages.title: How data centres became one of America’s hottest political issues
passages.passage:
How data centres became one of America’s hottest political issues
A little over a year ago some polls showed majority support for local data-centre construction. By March that had flipped: one Gallup poll found 71% opposed. Surveys by Annenberg recorded a 19-point swing in net favourability between February and June-July. An Economist/YouGov poll from the end of August put opposition at 63%. Data centres were viewed as bad for the country across every group of voters (see chart 1).
The growing opposition is sand in the wheels of the industry. Sales-tax exemptions for computer chips—the biggest cost of building a new data centre—remain in place in most states, including Texas. But they have been paused in others, including Arizona and Ohio, or made conditional, as in Pennsylvania. That, along with satisfying local demands, will inevitably increase the cost of new data centres. Even so, a handful of states still wield outsize influence. Texas alone has more data centres under construction than Georgia, Arizona and Pennsylvania combined (see chart 3).

High Court seeks timeline for steps toward Palestinians’ return to northern West Bank camps
The High Court of Justice on Sunday ordered the state to provide a timetable for completing the measures it says are needed before Palestinians displaced from three refugee camps in the northern West Bank can return to their homes, and to say whether that work can be accelerated.
The ruling came in a petition filed by six Palestinian residents and the Association for Civil Rights in Israel, which seeks to enable the residents’ return to their homes in the Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nur Shams refugee camps and to establish a mechanism for the return of other displaced residents. The petition also asks the state to provide for residents’ humanitarian needs until they can return.
Supreme Court President Isaac Amit and Justices Alex Stein and Khaled Kabub noted that about one year and nine months had passed since the start of Operation Iron Wall, the IDF operation launched in the northern West Bank back in January 2025. According to the state, the security conditions needed for residents to return had still not been met.

passages.passage:
Andhra Pradesh villages give a reality check to India’s 2030 malaria elimination target
All cells in the body, including tumour cells, shed DNA into the bloodstream when they die. Multi-cancer early detection tests look for the trace amounts of tumour DNA in the bloodstream. This circulating “cell-free” DNA contains information about what type of tissue it came from and whether it is normal or cancerous.
Multi-cancer early detection tests are different from existing liquid biopsies because they are trying to detect early-stage cancer, when there aren’t that many tumour cells yet. Detecting these cancer cells can be challenging early on because non-cancer cells also shed DNA into the bloodstream. Since most of the circulating DNA in the bloodstream comes from non-cancer cells, detecting the presence of a few molecules of cancer DNA is like finding a needle in a haystack.
Making things even more difficult, blood cells shed abnormal DNA naturally with ageing, and these strands can be confused for circulating cancer DNA. This phenomenon, known as clonal hematopoiesis, confounded early attempts at developing multi-cancer early detection tests, with too many false positive results.

Hours before polls opened for the US midterm elections, the FBI's New Haven field office told voters the wrong date for Election Day in a post promoting the bureau's work to protect the vote.
'Election day is Wednesday and the #FBI is working around the clock to ensure the midterms are safe,' the account wrote on X at about 4:00 p.m. ET on Monday, 2 November, roughly 14 hours before Connecticut's polling places opened.
Election Day is Tuesday, 3 November. Federal law fixes the general election on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, and Connecticut polls are open from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., according to the office of Governor Ned Lamont.
By late Monday, X users had attached a Community Note stating that Election Day falls on Tuesday, 3 November. Its second line read: 'Not Wednesday'.
New Haven, home to the FBI field office, is the only Connecticut municipality the Justice Department plans to monitor on Election Day, according to the Connecticut Secretary of the State's office. Two teams of two will check sites covered by federal Spanish-language assistance rules, state officials said.

On Tuesday morning, Connecticut's election chief, Stephanie Thomas, said the posts were misinformation and told voters to ignore them. Polls for the US midterms opened that day, 3 November.
The X post went up on Monday, 2 November. It pointed to a radio show where FBI staff talked about keeping the vote safe, but it named the wrong day. Within hours, users posted on X, pointing out that Election Day was Tuesday, not Wednesday. A Facebook copy followed at about 3am, the Yale Daily News reported. Journalist Ken Klippenstein shared a screenshot of the X post, and his message appears below.
Why is the FBI falsely telling people that the election is on Wednesday? https://t.co/AJYGo8xbKB
In September, FBI Director Kash Patel told senators that all 56 of the bureau's field offices had an election crimes community coordinator. FBI office’s wrong Election Day post on X prompts Connecticut correction
HARTFORD, Conn. — An FBI Election Day post from the bureau’s New Haven field office incorrectly told followers that voting would take place on Wednesday, prompting Connecticut’s top elections official to issue a public correction on the day polls were open and the bureau to remove the message.
The post, published on the official FBI New Haven X account on Nov. 2, said: “Election day is Wednesday and the #FBI is working around the clock to ensure the midterms are safe.” Federal Election Day in 2026 was Tuesday, Nov. 3. The FBI later said the post contained a typo and had been removed once the error was identified.
Thomas’s official statement identified the source directly: “We are aware of misinformation circulating on social media, posted by the FBI’s New Haven office, incorrectly stating that Election Day is Wednesday.” It then stated the correct date in unambiguous terms.

Jackson, a fifth-generation logger and former president of the Maine Senate, entered the race in July after the party’s original nominee, Graham Platner, withdrew. Troy Jackson. who is 58, and a former Maine Senate president and fifth-generation logger from rural northern Maine. Democrat Troy Jackson defeated Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine, ending her bid for a historic sixth term and handing Democrats a crucial seat in their push to retake the US Senate.

passages.passage:
Katie Zacharia out as White House press secretary after just 5 days on the job: Reports
Katie Zacharia, political commentator turned White House Press Secretary, has been let go of her role in the Donald Trump administration on Friday, the New York Times reported.
The NYT cited five people familiar with the matter to report that Zacharia has been let go from her White House role effective immediately. The report came moments after Trump said before boarding Air Force One Friday that he had asked Zacharia to “reconsider” if she wants to continue as the White House Press Secretary.
Zacharia became the White House Press Secretary on October 10. In her six days in office, she has faced intense media scrutiny over her bar credentials.
Zacharia's departure makes her the shortest-serving White House Press Secretary after Anthony Scaramucci, who served only 11 days as the White House Director of Communications in the previous Trump administration.
Zacharia's credentials to practise law in the United States were questioned after she described herself as a law-practitioner before entering politics. Trump, announcing her nomination to the role, referred to her as an "attorney".

Reuters initially reported that two White House officials said she had been “let go” following scrutiny of her briefings and legal background.
Newsweek emailed the White House for further comment on Saturday morning.
A press secretary speaks for the president and is expected to give accurate information under intense public scrutiny, making clarity about the circumstances of an incumbent’s departure significant.
Before Zacharia, a conservative commentator and former communications adviser for Trump Media & Technology Group, took office, the White House went 45 days without a press secretary following Karoline Leavitt’s August 27 departure.

Fed by heavy rains in Nepal, the Gandak river swelled to a record level on Tuesday, damaging embankments in the West Champarandistrict and threatening widespread inundation in Bihar already bruised by a massive flood.

Bihar was put on high alert on Wednesday as floodwaters from Nepal entered the Gandak river and reached the barrage, prompting the authorities concerned to open all 36 gates to control the surge.

The Pan American Health Organization’s decision signals a major public health setback for the US. Specialists said the fall in vaccination coverage began before President Donald Trump returned to office. However, experts added that recent policy changes and public remarks may have made matters worse. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said federal work would keep focusing on outbreak control.
CDC data showed falling measles-mumps-rubella vaccination rates among young children. In the 2025-26 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners got required MMR shots. The Foreign Ministry emphasized the importance of the decision in terms of bilateral relations between the two countries, opening the door to more business and cooperation.
According to Japanese media reports, Israel is now considered a "Level 2" destination, meaning the Japanese government advises against unnecessary travel, down from the previous "Level 3" designation, which called for refraining from travel entirely.

passages.title: Jute mill reopens after Arjun Singh’s intervention
passages.passage:
Kolkata: Around 2,000 workers heaved a sigh of relief as Alliance Mills (Lease) Ltd. at Jagatdal in North 24-Parganas reopened on Wednesday after remaining shut for nearly six months.
The jute mill had been closed since December 26, 2025, following a suspension of work notice. On Tuesday, a tripartite meeting involving the management and operating trade unions was held at the New Secretariat Buildings in Kolkata under the stewardship of Arjun Singh, Minister-in-Charge of the Labour Department, Bhaskar Bhattacharya, Minister of State for Labour, and Ashis Sarkar, Special Labour Commissioner.
“The issues were discussed at length and, after protracted deliberations, it was unanimously decided that the mill would resume operations from Wednesday,” a Labour Department official said.
The Labour Department has already initiated measures to facilitate the reopening of nine closed jute mills across the state, whose closure has left more than 18,000 workers without jobs. Singh recently reviewed the situation of the closed jute mills and took stock of developments from departmental officials. The affected mills are located in the districts of Howrah, Hooghly and North 24-Parganas.

Israel's president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a new government, Israeli media reported, following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power.
Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, is fighting to hold onto office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an October 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament.

Israel's President Isaac Herzog has chosen Gadi Eisenkot over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to try to form a new government.
Israel's President Isaac Herzog has chosen Gadi Eisenkot over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to try to form a new government. The decision came following a deadlocked election that left neither of the men winning a majority in the Knesset. Herzog's office confirmed that the Israeli president has informed Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, on Saturday night “of his intention to task him with forming a government”.
It noted that the formal appointment would take place in an official ceremony, scheduled to occur on Sunday at the president's residence in Jerusalem. “Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X in his first reaction to the announcement of his designation.

passages.title: Netanyahu faces ouster as Israeli president picks Eisenkot; defence minister sounds Iran alarm
passages.passage:
Netanyahu faces ouster as Israeli president picks Eisenkot; defence minister sounds Iran alarm
New Delhi: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced the prospect of losing power on Sunday after President Isaac Herzog formally tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country's next government, even as Defence Minister Israel Katz warned that Iran was renewing its efforts to acquire nuclear weapons and that Israel's military mission against Tehran remained unfinished.
Netanyahu, meanwhile, has called for a national unity government involving his Likud party and Eisenkot's alliance, while warning against a government supported by Arab parties, which he has accused of threatening Israel's security.
Eisenkot, who served as Israel's military chief between 2015 and 2019, joined Netanyahu's wartime government after the October 2023 Hamas attacks before leaving amid disagreements over the handling of the conflict.
If Eisenkot fails to form a coalition, Herzog could give Netanyahu an opportunity to assemble a government, while continued deadlock could lead to another general election.

passages.passage:
INDIA bloc supporters gather at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for 'Chalo Dilli' protest
Supporters of various INDIA bloc parties gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday for the Opposition alliance's 'Chalo Dilli' protest against alleged electoral irregularities and to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The leaders travelled in an open bus to Minto Road, from where the march to Ramlila Maidan was scheduled to begin around noon.
Ahead of the protest, Rahul Gandhi urged people travelling to Delhi to support local businesses by shopping from small traders in the run-up to Diwali, Chhath and Bhai Dooj. In a video message posted on X on Saturday, he said the rally would not hurt businesses and encouraged participants to combine their protest with shopping.
The INDIA bloc has estimated that up to 10 lakh people could attend the mobilisation, while Delhi Police expects around 50,000. Ramlila Maidan can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, but its effective capacity is expected to fall to 30,000-40,000 with chairs, enclosures and designated passageways in place. Additional space outside the ground has been earmarked for crowds.

passages.passage:
INDIA Bloc Supporters Converge At Ramlila Maidan; Rahul Calls For ‘Chalo Dilli’ March
New Delhi: Delhi saw a big opposition gathering on Sunday as workers and supporters of the INDIA bloc reached the capital for its “Chalo Dilli” protest. The alliance is demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and protesting alleged problems in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists, agencies reported.
People began arriving at Ramlila Maidan early in the morning. Samajwadi Party workers gathered outside party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s residence, while Congress supporters met at Himachal Bhawan and then moved towards the rally venue. Many supporters came from different states on Sunday, while others had reached Delhi on Saturday or earlier.
There is a big difference in turnout estimates. The INDIA bloc says up to 10 lakh people may join, while Delhi Police expects around 50,000. Ramlila Maidan can hold about 45,000–50,000 people when empty, but its capacity may fall to 30,000–40,000 because of chairs, barricades and passages. Space outside the ground has been kept for extra crowds.
